cards.text: Jesus just told a storm to calm down, and it did (Matthew 8:26). Now He lands on the other side, in the region of the Gadarenes. And somebody meets Him there, friend, and it is NOT a welcome committee.

cards.question: Jesus lands in the region of the Gadarenes. Who comes to meet Him?
Where are these two demon-possessed men coming from?
The two demon-possessed men from the tombs are so ___ that no one can pass that way.

cards.text: Then the two men start SHOUTING at Jesus. He JUST got off the boat, friend. Not even a "hello, how was the trip?"

cards.question: True or false: The two men shouting at Jesus know who He is.
The men shout a question at Jesus, the Son of God. Has He come here to do what?

answers.text: Torture them before the appointed time
Take over the tombs for Himself
Take them back across the sea

cards.text: Hold on. Back on the boat, the men just asked, "What kind of man is this?" (Matthew 8:27). And the demons are out here SHOUTING the answer: Son of God.
Meanwhile, in the distance, a large herd of pigs is feeding. Totally unbothered. Just a regular day at the office.

cards.question: The demons beg Jesus for something if He drives them out. What do they ask?

answers.text: Let them stay in the tombs

cards.question: True or false: Jesus answers the demons' request with a long speech.

cards.text: "Go!" He tells them, and they come out and go into the pigs. ONE word and they're GONE. Friend, I once spent a whole afternoon asking a fly to leave my bakery. The fly won.

cards.question: True or false: Once the demons go into the pigs, the whole herd rushes down the steep bank into the sea.

cards.text: The whole herd dies in the waters. Now picture being the guys tending those pigs, trying to explain THAT one.

cards.question: Those tending the pigs run off into the town. What do they report?

answers.text: Everything including what happened to the two men
Only that the whole herd was lost
That thieves had taken the herd away

cards.text: Then the WHOLE town goes out to meet Jesus. Everybody. Every last one.

cards.question: When the whole town sees Jesus, they beg Him to ___ their region.

cards.text: Jesus just set free two men nobody could get past. And the town looks right at Him and says, "Please. Just go."

findings.problem: The card says Jesus 'told a storm to calm down.' Matthew 8:26 says He rebuked the winds and the sea, and it was perfectly calm. 'Told... to calm down' renames what He did.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Card 1 uses Matthew 8:26 and card 8 uses Matthew 8:27. Both are from the previous passage and are referenced in the card text. But the cards' verses fields cite only Matthew 8:28 and Matthew 8:29. Citing 'from the first verse it uses to the last' would make the range start outside the passage, and for card 1 it would also take in 8:27, which card 1 doesn't use.
findings.question: When a story card uses a verse from outside the passage, should its verses field include that verse? Or is the inline reference in the text enough, with the field citing only the passage verses it tells?

findings.problem: Nothing on cards 5 or 6 lets the baker reason toward 'torture them before the appointed time.' The only way to get it right is luck or prior knowledge. It also asks the baker to come up with the content of the men's shout.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Take over the tombs for Himself' is odd next to the others and reads as close to silly.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Matthew 8:29 says 'they shouted,' and 'they' is the two demon-possessed men. The card says 'the demons are out here SHOUTING the answer.' It names a speaker the text doesn't name, and it doesn't match cards 5 to 7, which say the two men shout.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Leave them alone for now' can be argued from Matthew 8:29: 'What do You want with us... Have You come here to torture us before the appointed time?' A baker could say this is what the demons asked.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: No story card before this one sets up what happens to the herd. Card 12 stops at the demons going into the pigs. The rush down the steep bank into the sea is a pure 50/50 true or false. With cards 3, 6, 7 and 11 also leaning on discovery, too many choice cards here can't be reasoned out.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The town's words 'Please. Just go.' are in quotation marks and presented as what the town says. They aren't BSB wording. Matthew 8:34 only says they begged Him to leave their region. This is a paraphrase of the text, not a made-up joke line.

rule.text: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included. A paraphrase uses no quotation marks.

findings.problem: Card 18 retells Matthew 8:32 and 8:34, which cards 12, 16 and 17 already covered. It doesn't move the passage forward.

Outside card 12's fly joke and card 5's 'how was the trip' line, the voice is mostly mild. Cards 9, 14 and 16 ('Just a regular day at the office,' 'trying to explain THAT one,' 'Everybody. Every last one.') read as pleasant rather than laugh-out-loud. Big moments like the herd rushing into the sea and the whole town coming out have no real laugh.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
